I'm honestly not sure what to think. (and let me say, the old version ranked among my absolute favourites here)
On one side, the recovery log is rather great, as are other things you have done with this as per the rewrite.

On other side, the removal of this

827a: A warning to new researchers — when we talk so dispassionately about "anomalies" we're referring to things like the "broken-tooth tree". We put part of a jaw in the Soup, hoping we'd get something we could use in a reconstructive surgery experiment, and the Soup grew this central trunk of thick muscle tissue. We think that the muscle tissue was based on the tongue. From this central trunk partially constructed jaws grew. Rhythmic muscle moves would cause the jaws to open and snap shut. They did this over and over and over. By the time the Soup reset itself, the teeth were shattered, and we were clearing tooth pieces from the soup bowl filter on an hourly basis.

So, yeah, keep that in mind that's what an "anomaly" is. -Dr. ████████

note and the incredibly evocative imagery within for what is a single sentence description leaves me unable to leave my upvote on in good faith.

Neutral vote.

item.content:encoded:
I know old thread is months old, here, but yes, what you're thinking of is a bioreactor for cell production. In fact, here is a paper from PubMed about a stirred-suspension bioreactor for human embryonic stem cells—which these little guys resemble almost exactly. (The exception being hESCs prefer to be fed nutrient broth, not human organs.) In fact the very close resemblance to human stem cells exactly as they are in the real world makes me hesitant to vote on this, since while they are amazing, they're not precisely anomalous. The broken-tooth tree is the only thing in here that really screams "SCP" at me, and even then I'm not quite sold on 827 being something that needs containing just because it produces teratomas.

If it showed a strong tendency to agglutinate, climb out of its bioreactor, and eat people, then I might think of it as an SCP. Granted we've already got a lot of shambling gray goo SCPs, so it would need a different twist on why it's dangerous and weird than that.

Also dittoing the SOUP BOWL being a bit jarring. It's a stirred-suspension bioreactor; unless SOUP BOWL is some kind of acronym, there's no reason to give it a fancy all-caps name.

I was trying to get at something which would hold the broth, and keep it agitated at a constant temperature. It would also serve to feed nutrients and remove waste.

The SOUP BOWL was taken from some dim memories of an apparatus I saw at biofilm lab — since the cells you were incubating would form biofilm if stagnant, you had to keep the stuff moving to keep it in a liquid state, but it also basically had to do everything else an incubator did. Unfortunately, I don't remember the name of this device, otherwise I'd probably try to incorporate it.

/Edit:/ Unless I am misinformed, I believe a better word would be reactor, as in cell reactor.

item.content:encoded:
Okay… hmm. I think I have a few ideas.

Regarding what Djoric said about how there should be more science stuff, I don't think that the anomalies have to be all extreme like the tooth-tree. Say a high-profile doctor, or even a site director, had a bad liver and a rare blood type, and someone had the bright idea of putting part of his liver in the soup. Now, livers can be regrown from a small piece of itself, so when enough got made by the soup, it was transplanted in. However… the liver that the soup created belongs in a fetus rather than in an adult human. In a fetus, the liver is responsible for red blood cell production in mammals. Eventually, there's a large surplus of blood due to both liver and bone marrow producing blood cells, leading to a condition called polycythemia. In addition, it can't process alcohol at all, doesn't produce bile… the poor doctor eventually dies of this.

Regarding the crosstests…I've thought long and hard about this, and…. they're just silly. Firstly, there's no way an O5 would want to stick someone in an SCP just for the lulz. Secondly, these are human cells; why would 682 be even requested to be crosstested? And 963 isn't even organic, so unless some of Bright's spunk got on there, how would it count as a human organ? They make no sense.

At the same time, though… I do like the idea of a human accidentally falling into the SOUP BOWL and getting eaten, and reforming all wrong. But the only way I can think of it reforming incorrectly that would even be remotely original involves all of its tubing being "unfolded". Like, the brain being flattened out and unwrinkled, the intestines being stretched out to full length… but that almost sounds SCP-worthy in and of itself. I dunno.

Just my two cents.

item.content:encoded:
The tone here is abyssal. Short, simplistic sentences make it sound like it was written by a high school freshman who has yet to write anything longer than a page.

SCP-827 is a mass of biologically active cells. Genetic analysis, as well as analyses of the cell structure itself, indicates that these cells are human stem cells. These stem cells have both the properties of self-renewal and totipotency.

This could be combined into a single sentence.

"SCP-827 is a mass of biologically active human stem cells, capable of self-renewal and totipotency."

The thing with the test log is that there's no actual content. If you're going to put a crosstest in, give it purpose. A constant string of "denied by O5-x" and some "hurf durf Bright" is dumb. How about we see some actual science? The jawbone tree is good, but we need more of that. It is lolFoundation, and it is bad because it is used in the place of actual content.

Really, there's just loads of padding in this article and no real meat underneath.
